problem: Which of the following is a factor of ${u}^{2}-2u+5?$

feedback.problem: Which of the following is a factor of $-{v}^{2}+12v-45?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we let $f(v)=-{v}^{2}+12v-45.$

Next, we solve $f(v)=0$ by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(v) & =0 \\ -{v}^{2}+12v-45 & =0 \\ {v}^{2}-12v+45 & =0 \\ ({v}^{2}-2\cdot 6\cdot v+{6}^{2})-{6}^{2}+45 & =0 \\ (v-6)^{2}-36+45 & =0 \\ (v-6)^{2}+9 & =0 \\ (v-6)^{2} & =-9 \\ (v-6)^{2} & =9{\text{i}}^{2} \\ (v-6)^{2} & =(3\text{i})^{2} \\ v-6 & =\pm 3\text{i} \\ v & =6\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Since our quadratic equation has roots ${v}_{1}=6+3\text{i}$ and ${v}_{2}=6-3\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-1,$ the expression $-{v}^{2}+12v-45$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}-{v}^{2}+12v-45 & =a(v-{v}_{1})(v-{v}_{2}) \\  & =-(v-(6+3\text{i}))(v-(6-3\text{i})).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, among the given options, only $v-(6-3\text{i})$ is a factor of $-{v}^{2}+12v-45.$
